title: Redwood migration demo: OpenAI/Anthropic/Together parity mapping

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Carter (Redwood AE), Daniel Wu (Redwood SE), Ethan Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Acme CTO), Liam O'Connor (Acme ML Eng), Priya Singh (Acme DevOps), Noah Reed (Acme Product)

Summary (auto): Redwood walked through migration path from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood API covering parity mapping, console rollout options, and Optimize features; agreed to run a pilot and share benchmark artifacts.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood, this is Daniel and Ethan on the engineering side. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Maya: Good, thanks. we wanted a concrete look at how we map our current OpenAI + Anthropic calls to Redwood, plus see the console for rollouts.
[00:22] Daniel: Great — we'll start with API parity mapping, then show Console and Optimize. we'll highlight common gotchas — stop sequences, streaming behavior, embeddings norms, and kv cache behavior for chat.
[00:35] Liam: quick context — we use OpenAI for chat completions and Together for some internal fine-tuned models; Anthropic for assistant-style safety filters. main constraints: latency under 300ms P50 for short prompts, and encryption with KMS is mandatory.
[00:52] Ethan: okay noted; can you share typical request shapes? temperature ranges, max_tokens, are you using function calls?
[01:05] Noah: mostly temperature 0.0-0.7, max_tokens 150-400, some function/tool calling for entity extraction, and embeddings at 1536 dims.
[01:18] Daniel: cool — we'll show parameter mappings. first, the basic text gen parity: OpenAI's temperature -> Redwood temperature, max_tokens -> max_tokens, stop sequences -> stop, top_p/nucleus sampling handled similarly. one difference: Redwood returns a streaming delta with token_type metadata by default, some customers see slight punctuation diffs from OpenAI. transcription note: sometimes the generated punctuation is slightly different in streaming.
[01:45] Maya: any differences in rate limiting or quotas? we have bursty traffic during sync jobs.
[01:52] Sofia: hosted API has quotas and rate limits you control in Console; for predictable bursts we recommend Dedicated or burst-capacity config. we'll show autoscaling policies in the Console shortly.
[02:10] [02:10] Daniel: about function / tool calling parity — Redwood supports structured function outputs and JSON schema enforcement similar to OpenAI's tool calling; for Together-style custom fine-tunes we map your endpoint to Redwood model variants and attach model-specific params (temperature, sampling, penalty).
[02:35] Liam: what about embeddings? are they 1:1 with OpenAI/Anthropic dims, and will our existing vector DBs accept them?
[02:43] Daniel: yes, Redwood exposes embeddings endpoints that match common dimensionalities and we document the model->dim mapping. we provide a quick mapping spreadsheet for the models and recommended distance metrics. you'll likely need to run a quick re-embed check, but in many cases the dims and similarity semantics are comparable.
[03:05] Ethan: small caveat: quantized model profiles can change decimal-level similarity, Optimize recommends reindexing thresholds after switching to a quantized runtime.
[03:20] Maya: security — SOC2, SAML/SSO, and KMS. we need to know if keys stay in our control.
[03:30] Sofia: Redwood Private and Dedicated support customer-managed KMS integrations and HSM via enterprise plans. for hosted, we offer KMS integrations and customer key options; we'll send the security pack. we are SOC2 compliant and can share attestations.
[03:50] Priest? (transcription glitch)
[03:55] Priya: yes just to add — our infra team will want a VPC/private deployment option for pilot.
[04:02] Sofia: that's supported — we do VPC endpoints and private control plane for Private deployments. we'll include VPC network setup docs.
[04:15] [04:15] Demo start - small API example
[04:18] Daniel: I'll share my screen — here's a simple parity snippet: OpenAI call -> Redwood call. same HTTP/SDK patterns, most fields identical. e.g., OpenAI: {"model": "gpt-4", "messages": [...], "temperature": 0.2} -> Redwood: {"model": "redwood-4x" , "messages": [...], "temperature": 0.2}.
[04:45] Liam: so we don't have to rewrite large parts of the client. good.
[04:50] Daniel: yes, in many cases it's a drop-in change. there are edge cases: Together uses different role tagging in chat sometimes and Anthropic has assistant/human tokens naming, Redwood normalizes but your prompt templates might need small changes.
[05:10] [05:10] Screen: Console overview
[05:12] Ethan: in Console you can pin model versions, create rollouts (canary/A-B), and set automatic fallback policies. here's a rollout where 10% traffic goes to a trimmed quantized variant and 90% to full precision.
[05:30] Maya: can we do time-based rollouts and automatic rollback on latency spikes?
[05:35] Ethan: yes, you can set SLO thresholds and automatic rollback; tracing hooks help debug failing prompts.
[05:42] Noah: what's the visibility on cost per token?
[05:46] Sofia: Console shows token-level cost and latency breakdown by route and model; Optimize also surfaces actionable recommendations to reduce cost like batching and aggressive kv caching for common prefixes.
[06:02] [06:02] Optimize discussion
[06:05] Daniel: Optimize's recommendations include batching windows, quant profiles per model, and pre-warmed KV-cache for common session continuations. these can reduce unit cost by 30-60% depending on workload.
[06:20] Liam: do you support dynamic batching on Dedicated GPUs without adding latency? we're sensitive to P50 latency.
[06:28] Daniel: our runtime supports continuous batching tuned to latency SLOs — it will batch only when it observes beneficial aggregation for throughput, and we have per-route latency overrides so critical routes can bypass large batching.
[06:40] Priya: are there hardware constraints for pilot — do we need GPUs on our side?
[06:46] Sofia: for hosted and Dedicated, Redwood manages GPUs; for Private on-prem we can ship an on-prem package, but most pilots use our hosted/Dedicated footprints.
[06:58] [07:00] Parity specifics: stop sequences & streaming differences
[07:02] Daniel: important parity note — stop sequences behave slightly differently across vendors when combined with streaming. we added an explicit stop token post-processing stage to align behavior; we'll share example test prompts to validate parity.
[07:20] Maya: great — we need that since our UI relies on stop tokens for chunking.
[07:26] [08:00] Demo: Function calling
[08:03] Ethan: here's a function call demo; Redwood returns the structured JSON in the same block and also emits a separate function_called event for observability. you can capture the function name and args the same way.
[08:18] Liam: any latency penalty for function calls?
[08:22] Daniel: negligible; the extra event is emitted from the runtime. it helps debugging and tracing across services.
[08:32] [09:00] Demo: Embeddings workflow
[09:05] Daniel: embeddings endpoints behave similarly. we recommend running an A/B of embeddings with your nearest neighbor index and comparing recall to your current embeddings. for semantically-sensitive applications re-embedding is often advised.
[09:22] Priya: our privacy policy requires we purge raw inputs after embedding, is there a retention control?
[09:29] Sofia: yes — we provide data retention controls and can configure no-logs for sensitive routes in Dedicated/Private. we'll share the retention policy doc.
[09:42] [10:00] Performance & benchmarks
[10:05] Daniel: we recommend a 3-phase pilot: small pilot to validate API parity, a throughput benchmark with your sample prompts, then an end-to-end integration test. we'll provide a benchmark harness and a model mapping spreadsheet.
[10:20] Maya: how long to stand up a pilot?
[10:24] Sofia: often 1-2 weeks for a basic pilot (hosted), 3-4 for Dedicated or VPC prep. depends on compliance steps.
[10:32] [11:30] Cost discussion
[11:34] Liam: cost vs OpenAI — is Redwood cheaper for token-heavy workloads?
[11:38] Sofia: depends on model and quantization. Optimize can reduce cost substantially; Dedicated reserved capacity is best for predictable throughput. we'll include example unit economics based on your usage patterns.
[11:50] [12:00] Security deep-dive preview
[12:05] Sofia: we'll schedule a security review with our security engineering — they can go through SOC2 artifacts, SAML setup, KMS key exchange, and network diagrams.
[12:18] Priya: we'll need a contact for VPC peering and the network CIDR exchange.
[12:23] Ethan: I'll be point on the infra network docs.
[12:30] [13:30] Questions from Acme
[13:32] Noah: does Redwood support custom fine-tunes or only model variants?
[13:37] Daniel: Redwood supports hosting customer fine-tunes/weights as model variants in Dedicated/Private; for hosted we have curated variants and a model onboarding path. for Together-fine-tuned models we can import weights with proper licensing.
[13:54] Maya: do you provide any guardrails for safety filters like Anthropic?
[13:58] Sofia: yes, we offer safety tooling and can integrate third-party safety chains, also you can route to safety models as a pre-check.
[14:12] [17:00] Transcript hiccup - speaker overlap (short)
[17:05] Speaker 1: uh yeah, so when we change the model, do we also need to retrain our prompt templates?
[17:12] Daniel: usually minor tweaks; Optimize suggests small temperature/top_p changes and sometimes explicit system prompts to match tone.
[17:25] [22:00] Console specifics: rollouts + tracing
[22:05] Ethan: here's a tracing example for a failing prompt, you can see token-by-token latency, model knee points, and where a fallback kicked in to the lower-cost variant.
[22:20] Liam: useful. can we export traces to our logging system?
[22:24] Ethan: yes — we push traces to customer configured sinks (S3, GCS, or SIEM).
[22:35] [26:00] Billing & contractual notes
[26:05] Sofia: for pilots we often do a short-term credit-backed pilot agreement; for Dedicated we propose a reserved commit. legal/procurement topics can be parallelized.
[26:28] Maya: procurement will need SLAs in the contract.
[26:32] Sofia: we have SLA templates and can add uptime and latency SLOs for Dedicated.
[27:00] [31:00] Final recap & next steps
[31:05] Sofia: quick recap: we'll send the parity spreadsheet, pricing/pilot agreement, and security pack. Daniel will share the model-mapping examples and benchmark harness. Acme to provide prompts and infra contact for VPC. next meeting: pilot kickoff — we'll aim for the week of 2026-07-13.
[31:30] Maya: that works for us. thanks, this was helpful.
[31:36] Noah: can you also include example code snippets for embeddings + vector db ingest?
[31:40] Daniel: yes, included in the model mapping repo we'll share.
[31:45] Priya: I'll send the sample corpus and a list of endpoints we plan to migrate.
[31:48] Sofia: perfect. action items in chat as well.
[32:00] [End of transcript — recording ends at 32 minutes in capture; meeting continued informally for Q&A off-record for ~10 minutes]

Notes: transcription contains minor speaker attribution errors and occasional dropped words as typical of automated transcripts.
